biomarkers.name: Non-HDL Cholesterol Test
biomarkers.description: All cholesterol except good cholesterol; includes LDL, VLDL, and other atherogenic particles that contribute to plaque buildup and cardiovascular disease.

biomarkers.name: HDL Cholesterol Test
biomarkers.description: Good cholesterol that helps remove bad cholesterol from arteries; higher levels are protective against heart disease.

biomarkers.name: Triglycerides Test
biomarkers.description: A type of fat in blood; high levels increase risk of heart disease and pancreatitis.

biomarkers.name: LDL Cholesterol Test
biomarkers.description: Bad cholesterol that can build up in arteries; high levels increase risk of heart disease and stroke.

biomarkers.name: Cholesterol/HDL Ratio Testing
biomarkers.description: The Castelli Risk Index I reflects the balance between all circulating cholesterol and protective HDL; lower values indicate healthier lipid profiles and reduced cardiovascular risk.

biomarkers.name: LDL/HDL Ratio Testing
biomarkers.description: The Castelli Risk Index II compares bad cholesterol to good cholesterol; provides targeted insight into the balance between atherogenic and protective lipoproteins.

biomarkers.name: Cholesterol, Total Test
biomarkers.description: The total amount of cholesterol in blood; high levels increase risk of heart disease.

biomarkers.name: Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) Testing
biomarkers.description: A protein that carries bad cholesterol; elevated levels increase risk of cardiovascular disease.

biomarkers.name: Lipoprotein (a) Testing
biomarkers.description: A type of lipoprotein associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular diseases.

biomarkers.name: Neutrophil-to-HDL Cholesterol Ratio (NHR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Integrates immune activation and lipid protection; elevated ratios are strongly associated with cardiovascular events, mortality, and systemic inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Triglyceride / HDL Cholesterol (Molar Ratio) Testing
biomarkers.description: A powerful marker of insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome; elevated ratios suggest metabolic dysfunction and increased cardiovascular risk.

biomarkers.name: Atherogenic Index of Plasma (AIP) Testing
biomarkers.description: Calculated as the logarithm of triglycerides to HDL ratio; reflects lipid quality and predicts cardiovascular risk compared with individual lipid markers.

biomarkers.name: Atherogenic Coefficient Test
biomarkers.description: Shows the ratio of potentially harmful cholesterol to protective HDL; higher values indicate increased risk of plaque formation and inflammation.

biomarkers.name: LDL Cholesterol / Total Cholesterol (Mass Ratio) Testing
biomarkers.description: Expresses the proportion of total cholesterol made up of LDL; higher ratios indicate greater cardiovascular risk as more cholesterol is in atherogenic particles.

biomarkers.name: LDL-C / ApoB Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects cholesterol content per LDL particle and serves as a marker of particle size; low ratios indicate small, dense, more atherogenic LDL particles.

biomarkers.name: Uric Acid / HDL-C Testing
biomarkers.description: Compares uric acid levels to protective HDL cholesterol; elevated ratios may indicate increased metabolic and cardiovascular risk.

biomarkers.name: TG / ApoB Testing
biomarkers.description: Provides insight into lipoprotein particle size and composition; low ratios suggest small, dense LDL particles that are more atherogenic.

biomarkers.name: Non-HDL Cholesterol / Apolipoprotein B (Non-HDL-C / ApoB) Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects cholesterol content per atherogenic particle; low ratios suggest cholesterol-poor, small dense particles linked to increased cardiovascular risk.

biomarkers.name: Lipoprotein fractionation Test
biomarkers.description: Breaks down cholesterol into particle types to assess heart health risk.

biomarkers.name: ADMA Test
biomarkers.description: Measures blood vessel function and nitric oxide balance for vascular health.

biomarkers.name: SDMA Test
biomarkers.description: Measures blood vessel function and nitric oxide balance for vascular health.

biomarkers.name: Free T4 Index (T7) Testing
biomarkers.description: Estimates free thyroid hormone levels; helps assess thyroid function more accurately.

biomarkers.name: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH) Testing
biomarkers.description: A molecule that acts like a messenger, telling your thyroid gland how much hormone to produce; abnormal levels can signal an underactive or overactive thyroid.

biomarkers.name: T3 Uptake Test
biomarkers.description: Measures thyroid hormone binding proteins; helps interpret thyroid function tests.

biomarkers.name: Thyroxine (T4), Total Testing
biomarkers.description: The main thyroid hormone; abnormal levels indicate overactive or underactive thyroid.

biomarkers.name: Thyroid peroxidase antibody Test
biomarkers.description: Antibodies that attack the thyroid; presence indicates autoimmune thyroid disease.

biomarkers.name: Thyroglobulin Antibodies Test
biomarkers.description: Antibodies against thyroid protein; may indicate autoimmune thyroid conditions.

biomarkers.name: Triiodothyronine (T3), Free Testing
biomarkers.description: The active form of thyroid hormone; more accurately reflects thyroid function than total T3.

biomarkers.name: Glucose Test
biomarkers.description: Blood sugar level; elevated levels may indicate diabetes or prediabetes.

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) Testing
biomarkers.description: Average blood sugar over 2-3 months; used to diagnose and monitor diabetes.

biomarkers.name: Estimated Average Glucose (mmol/L) Testing
biomarkers.description: Converts HbA1c into estimated average blood glucose over 2-3 months in mmol/L units; reflects long-term glycemic control and metabolic health.

biomarkers.name: Estimated Average Glucose (mg/dL) Testing
biomarkers.description: Converts HbA1c into estimated average blood glucose over 2-3 months; provides an intuitive measure of long-term glucose control in familiar glucose meter units.

biomarkers.name: Uric Acid Test
biomarkers.description: A waste product that can form crystals in joints; high levels may cause gout or kidney stones.

biomarkers.name: Insulin Test
biomarkers.description: A hormone that regulates blood sugar; elevated levels may indicate insulin resistance or diabetes risk.

biomarkers.name: Corrected Calcium (Albumin-adjusted) Testing
biomarkers.description: Adjusts total calcium based on albumin levels to estimate biologically active calcium; accounts for protein binding effects on calcium measurement.

biomarkers.name: (Triglyceride - Glucose Index) - TyG Index Testing
biomarkers.description: Estimates insulin resistance using fasting triglycerides and glucose; higher values suggest metabolic dysfunction and increased diabetes risk.

biomarkers.name: Leptin Test
biomarkers.description: Regulates hunger and body weight balance.

biomarkers.name: Cardio IQ Insulin Resistance Test
biomarkers.description: Assesses how well your body processes insulin and glucose.

biomarkers.name: Adiponectin Test
biomarkers.description: A hormone that improves insulin sensitivity and fat metabolism.

biomarkers.name: Fructosamine Test
biomarkers.description: Shows average blood sugar control over the past few weeks.

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin
biomarkers.description: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen; low levels indicate anemia while high levels may suggest dehydration or lung conditions.

biomarkers.name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin (MCH) Testing
biomarkers.description: The average amount of hemoglobin in each red blood cell; useful for diagnosing different types of anemia.

biomarkers.name: Hematocrit Test
biomarkers.description: The percentage of blood volume made up of red blood cells; helps assess for anemia, dehydration, or blood disorders.

biomarkers.name: Red Blood Cells (RBC) Testing
biomarkers.description: Cells that carry oxygen throughout your body; low levels may indicate anemia while high levels may suggest dehydration or lung disease.

biomarkers.name: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) Testing
biomarkers.description: The average size of red blood cells; helps classify different types of anemia and nutritional deficiencies.

biomarkers.name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration (MCHC) Testing
biomarkers.description: The concentration of hemoglobin in red blood cells; helps identify specific types of anemia and blood disorders.

biomarkers.name: Platelet Count Test
biomarkers.description: Blood cells responsible for clotting; low levels increase bleeding risk while high levels may increase clotting risk.

biomarkers.name: Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW) Testing
biomarkers.description: Measures variation in red blood cell size; elevated levels may indicate nutritional deficiencies or blood disorders.

biomarkers.name: Mean Platelet Volume (MPV) Testing
biomarkers.description: The average size of platelets; helps assess platelet function and bone marrow activity.

biomarkers.name: Protein, Total Test
biomarkers.description: The total amount of proteins in blood; abnormal levels may indicate liver disease, kidney disease, or nutritional problems.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin D, 25-Hydroxy Test
biomarkers.description: The storage form of vitamin D; low levels may cause bone problems, muscle weakness, and immune dysfunction.

biomarkers.name: RDW / MCV Ratio Testing
biomarkers.description: Compares red cell size variation to average cell size; helps characterize different types of anemia and red blood cell disorders.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin C Test
biomarkers.description: Boosts immunity, collagen production, and recovery from stress or exercise.

biomarkers.name: Selenium Test
biomarkers.description: Antioxidant that protects cells and supports thyroid and immune health.

biomarkers.name: Magnesium Test
biomarkers.description: Supports muscle recovery, energy production, and relaxation.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin K Test
biomarkers.description: Important for bone strength and normal blood clotting.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin E Test
biomarkers.description: Protects cells and supports heart, skin, and reproductive health.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) Testing
biomarkers.description: Supports energy, nerve function, and red blood cell health.

biomarkers.name: Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) Testing
biomarkers.description: An enzyme found in liver and bones; elevated levels may indicate liver disease or bone disorders.

biomarkers.name: Albumin/Globulin Ratio Testing
biomarkers.description: Compares albumin to globulin proteins; helps assess liver function, protein metabolism, and immune status.

biomarkers.name: Albumin Test
biomarkers.description: The main protein in blood that maintains fluid balance; low levels may indicate liver disease, kidney disease, or malnutrition.

biomarkers.name: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) Testing
biomarkers.description: A liver enzyme; elevated levels indicate liver damage or disease.

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin, Total Test
biomarkers.description: A waste product from red blood cell breakdown; elevated levels may indicate liver disease or blood disorders.

biomarkers.name: Globulin Test
biomarkers.description: Blood proteins including antibodies; abnormal levels may indicate immune disorders, liver disease, or infections.

biomarkers.name: Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) Testing
biomarkers.description: An enzyme found in liver and muscles; elevated levels may indicate liver damage or muscle injury.

biomarkers.name: Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase (GGT) Testing
biomarkers.description: A liver enzyme sensitive to alcohol and bile duct problems; elevated levels may indicate liver disease.

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin, Direct Test
biomarkers.description: The processed form of bilirubin; elevated levels may indicate liver disease or bile duct problems.

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin, Indirect Test
biomarkers.description: The unprocessed form of bilirubin; elevated levels may indicate blood disorders or liver problems.

biomarkers.name: Non-HDL Cholesterol / Total Cholesterol (Mass Ratio) Testing
biomarkers.description: Measures the proportion of total cholesterol carried by potentially harmful lipoproteins; higher ratios indicate increased atherosclerotic risk.

biomarkers.name: GGT-to-HDL Cholesterol Ratio (GGT / HDL-C) Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects the balance between oxidative stress and lipid protection; elevated ratios suggest liver stress and increased cardiometabolic risk.

biomarkers.name: Indirect-to-Direct Bilirubin Ratio (I/D Bilirubin Ratio) Testing
biomarkers.description: Compares unconjugated to conjugated bilirubin; helps differentiate between hemolytic disorders and liver dysfunction.

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin-to-Albumin Ratio (BAR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Assesses the relationship between bilirubin levels and albumin; useful for evaluating liver synthetic function and bilirubin metabolism.

biomarkers.name: BUN/Creatinine Ratio Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects the relationship between urea and creatinine waste products; helps distinguish between dehydration, blood loss, kidney dysfunction, or liver issues.

biomarkers.name: Calcium Test
biomarkers.description: Essential mineral for bones, muscles, and nerves; abnormal levels may indicate bone disease, kidney problems, or hormonal disorders.

biomarkers.name: Potassium Test
biomarkers.description: An electrolyte essential for heart and muscle function; abnormal levels can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems.

biomarkers.name: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Testing
biomarkers.description: Measures bicarbonate levels in blood; helps assess acid-base balance and kidney function.

biomarkers.name: Creatinine Test
biomarkers.description: A waste product filtered by kidneys; elevated levels indicate decreased kidney function.

biomarkers.name: Chloride Test
biomarkers.description: An electrolyte that helps maintain fluid balance; abnormal levels may indicate kidney problems or dehydration.

biomarkers.name: Sodium Test
biomarkers.description: An electrolyte that helps maintain fluid balance; abnormal levels may indicate kidney problems or dehydration.

biomarkers.name: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Estimates how well kidneys filter waste; lower values indicate decreased kidney function.

biomarkers.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) Testing
biomarkers.description: A waste product filtered by kidneys; elevated levels indicate decreased kidney function.

biomarkers.name: Urine Color
biomarkers.description: Reflects hydration status, urine concentration, and overall fluid balance.

biomarkers.name: Urine Appearance
biomarkers.description: Shows urine clarity and color, reflecting hydration and internal balance.

biomarkers.name: Urine Specific Gravity
biomarkers.description: Reflects urine concentration, hydration status, and kidney function.

biomarkers.name: Urinary pH
biomarkers.description: Measures how acidic or alkaline urine is, reflecting acid-base balance.

biomarkers.name: Urinary Glucose
biomarkers.description: Measures glucose in urine, reflecting recent blood sugar levels.

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures bilirubin pigment in urine, reflecting liver or bile flow.

biomarkers.name: Ketones, Urine
biomarkers.description: Shows ketones from fat-burning as an alternative fuel.

biomarkers.name: Occult Blood, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures tiny amounts of blood in urine.

biomarkers.name: Protein, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures protein leakage in urine, reflecting kidney filtering health.

biomarkers.name: Nitrite, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures urine nitrites linked to certain urinary bacteria.

biomarkers.name: Leukocyte Esterase, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures white blood cell enzyme levels in urine.

biomarkers.name: WBC, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures white blood cells in urine, reflecting urinary tract inflammation.

biomarkers.name: RBC, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures red blood cells in urine, reflecting urinary tract lining integrity.

biomarkers.name: Epithelial Cells, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures shed urinary tract cells, reflecting urinary health or contamination.

biomarkers.name: Bacteria, Urine
biomarkers.description: Measures bacteria present in urine, linked to urinary tract infection.

biomarkers.name: High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein (hs-CRP) Testing
biomarkers.description: A marker of inflammation; elevated levels increase risk of heart disease and other inflammatory conditions.

biomarkers.name: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Measures how quickly red blood cells settle; elevated levels indicate inflammation or infection.

biomarkers.name: Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) Testing
biomarkers.description: Composite marker using platelets, neutrophils, and lymphocytes; reflects immune imbalance and systemic inflammation linked to cardiovascular risk.

biomarkers.name: Ferritin-to-Albumin Ratio (FAR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Compares iron storage protein to albumin; helps assess nutritional status and inflammatory burden in complex clinical scenarios.

biomarkers.name: Monocyte-to-HDL Ratio (MHR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Balances immune activation against lipid protection; elevated ratios indicate increased inflammation and reduced cardiovascular protection.

biomarkers.name: CRP / Albumin Ratio (CAR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Compares inflammatory marker to nutritional protein; elevated ratios indicate systemic inflammation with potential nutritional compromise.

biomarkers.name: Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Test
biomarkers.description: Reflects inflammatory and thrombotic status; elevated ratios may indicate increased cardiovascular risk and systemic inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Systemic Inflammation Response Index (SIRI) Testing
biomarkers.description: Composite inflammatory marker using neutrophils, monocytes, and lymphocytes; indicates systemic inflammatory burden.

biomarkers.name: Insulin-Like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1) Testing
biomarkers.description: A hormone that promotes growth and tissue repair; levels reflect growth hormone activity.

biomarkers.name: Health Score Test
biomarkers.description:
Feeling run down, foggy, or just off? Could a comprehensive look at your health help you understand why?
Your Health Score combines key biomarkers into a single number to show how your body is functioning. It simplifies complex data into a clear status update.
Tracking this score helps you understand the root of your fatigue without the guesswork. You gain the insight needed to improve your vitality and feel your best.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin B12 Test
biomarkers.description: Essential vitamin for nerve function and red blood cell formation; deficiency causes anemia and neurological problems.

biomarkers.name: Homocysteine Test
biomarkers.description: An amino acid that can damage blood vessels; elevated levels increase risk of heart disease and stroke.

biomarkers.name: Folate Test
biomarkers.description: A B vitamin essential for DNA synthesis and red blood cell formation; deficiency causes anemia and birth defects.

biomarkers.name: Folate, RBC Test
biomarkers.description: Shows long-term folate stores for DNA and cellular health.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin B6 (Plasma) Testing
biomarkers.description: Supports metabolism, energy, and neurotransmitter production.

biomarkers.name: Methylmalonic Acid (MMA) Testing
biomarkers.description: Detects vitamin B12 deficiency at the cellular level.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) Testing
biomarkers.description: Supports energy, nerve function, and red blood cell health.

biomarkers.name: Ferritin Test
biomarkers.description: A protein that stores iron; low levels indicate iron deficiency while high levels may indicate iron overload or inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Cortisol Test
biomarkers.description: The stress hormone; abnormal levels may indicate adrenal disorders or chronic stress.

biomarkers.name: Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC) Testing
biomarkers.description: Measures the blood's capacity to bind iron; helps diagnose iron deficiency or overload.

biomarkers.name: Iron Saturation Test
biomarkers.description: The percentage of iron-binding sites that are occupied; helps assess iron status and storage.

biomarkers.name: Iron, Total Test
biomarkers.description: Essential mineral for oxygen transport; low levels cause anemia while high levels may indicate iron overload.

biomarkers.name: BMI Test
biomarkers.description:
Struggling with low energy or joint pain, and wondering if checking your BMI could help?
BMI uses your height and weight to indicate if you are in a healthy range. It gives you a clear starting point.
Measuring this helps reveal if weight is contributing to your discomfort. You can then take steps to feel lighter and more energetic.

biomarkers.name: White Blood Cells (WBC) Testing
biomarkers.description: Immune system cells that help fight infections and diseases; abnormal levels may indicate infection, immune disorders, or blood cancers.

biomarkers.name: Eosinophils, Absolute Test
biomarkers.description: The actual number of eosinophils in your blood; useful for diagnosing allergic conditions and parasitic infections.

biomarkers.name: Lymphocytes, Absolute Test
biomarkers.description: The actual number of lymphocytes in your blood; important for evaluating immune system health.

biomarkers.name: Lymphocytes Test
biomarkers.description: White blood cells that fight viral infections and produce antibodies; levels help assess immune system function.

biomarkers.name: Basophils, Absolute Test
biomarkers.description: The actual number of basophils in your blood; helps evaluate allergic reactions and certain blood conditions.

biomarkers.name: Monocytes, Absolute Test
biomarkers.description: The actual number of monocytes in your blood; helps assess immune response and inflammatory conditions.

biomarkers.name: Neutrophils Test
biomarkers.description: White blood cells that fight bacterial infections; elevated levels often indicate bacterial infection or inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Monocytes Test
biomarkers.description: White blood cells that fight infections and remove dead cells; elevated levels may indicate chronic infection or inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Eosinophils Test
biomarkers.description: White blood cells that fight parasites and are involved in allergic reactions; elevated levels may indicate allergies or parasitic infections.

biomarkers.name: Basophils Test
biomarkers.description: White blood cells involved in allergic reactions and inflammation; elevated levels may indicate allergic conditions or blood disorders.

biomarkers.name: Neutrophils, Absolute Test
biomarkers.description: The actual number of neutrophils in your blood; helps assess immune function and infection risk.

biomarkers.name: Lymphocyte-to-Monocyte Ratio (LMR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects immune balance and inflammatory status; lower ratios may indicate chronic inflammation or immune dysfunction.

biomarkers.name: Platelet-to-WBC Ratio Test
biomarkers.description: Compares platelet count to total white blood cells; provides insight into hematologic balance and potential inflammatory states.

biomarkers.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Test
biomarkers.description: A marker of systemic inflammation and immune stress; elevated ratios are associated with increased cardiovascular risk and mortality.

biomarkers.name: Monocyte-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (MLR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects balance between innate and adaptive immunity; elevated ratios may indicate chronic inflammatory conditions.

biomarkers.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte & Platelet Ratio (NLPR) Testing
biomarkers.description: Advanced inflammatory marker combining multiple immune cell types; reflects complex immune-inflammatory interactions.

biomarkers.name: dsDNA antibody Test
biomarkers.description: Detects antibodies highly specific to lupus; rising levels often indicate increased disease activity, especially in the kidneys.

biomarkers.name: Rheumatoid factor
biomarkers.description: Helps identify rheumatoid arthritis or chronic joint inflammation.

biomarkers.name: CCP antibody Test
biomarkers.description: Identifies antibodies strongly tied to rheumatoid arthritis risk and progression.

biomarkers.name: ANA (antinuclear antibody) Testing
biomarkers.description: Screens for autoimmune activity often associated with lupus and related connective tissue diseases.

biomarkers.name: Celiac Disease Comprehensive Panel Testing
biomarkers.description: Screens for antibodies that indicate celiac-related autoimmunity and gluten-triggered immune activity.

biomarkers.name: Testosterone, Total Test
biomarkers.description: The primary male hormone; affects muscle mass, bone density, mood, and sexual function.

biomarkers.name: Sex Hormone Binding Globulin (SHBG) Testing
biomarkers.description: A protein that binds sex hormones; affects the amount of active hormones available to tissues.

biomarkers.name: Testosterone, Bioavailable Test
biomarkers.description: Testosterone that is available for use by tissues; includes free and loosely bound testosterone.

biomarkers.name: DHEA Sulfate (DHEA-S) Testing
biomarkers.description: A hormone precursor that declines with age; low levels may affect energy, mood, and immune function.

biomarkers.name: Testosterone, Free Test
biomarkers.description: The active form of testosterone not bound to proteins; more accurately reflects hormone activity.

biomarkers.name: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) Testing
biomarkers.description: A hormone that regulates reproductive function; levels help assess fertility and menopause status.

biomarkers.name: Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA), Free Testing
biomarkers.description: The unbound form of PSA; helps distinguish between benign and malignant prostate conditions.

biomarkers.name: Progesterone Test
biomarkers.description: A hormone important for menstrual cycle and pregnancy; levels help assess reproductive health.

biomarkers.name: Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA), Total Testing
biomarkers.description: A protein produced by the prostate; elevated levels may indicate prostate problems including cancer.

biomarkers.name: Luteinizing Hormone (LH) Testing
biomarkers.description: A hormone that triggers ovulation and testosterone production; helps assess reproductive health.

biomarkers.name: Prolactin Test
biomarkers.description: A hormone that stimulates milk production; abnormal levels may affect fertility and sexual function.

biomarkers.name: Free Androgen Index (FAI) Testing
biomarkers.description: Estimates biologically active testosterone by comparing total testosterone to SHBG; useful for assessing androgen status in both men and women.

biomarkers.name: Testosterone / Estradiol (T:E2) Testing
biomarkers.description: Reflects hormonal balance between androgens and estrogens; imbalances are linked to cardiovascular risk, inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction.

biomarkers.name: 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) Test
biomarkers.description: Evaluates adrenal and ovarian hormone balance affecting cycles and fertility.

biomarkers.name: Estradiol
biomarkers.description: Measures estrogen levels to assess ovarian function and hormone balance.

biomarkers.name: Mercury, blood Test
biomarkers.description: Screens for mercury exposure that may affect hormones and fertility.

biomarkers.name: Cardio IQ Insulin Test
biomarkers.description: Measures fasting insulin to assess blood sugar balance and metabolic health.

biomarkers.name: Thyroid antibodies Test
biomarkers.description: Detects thyroid autoimmunity that can impact metabolism and fertility.

biomarkers.name: Glucose, plasma Test
biomarkers.description: Checks blood sugar levels related to energy and metabolic balance.

biomarkers.name: AMH (anti-Müllerian hormone) Testing
biomarkers.description: Key marker of ovarian reserve and remaining egg count.

biomarkers.name: Ultra-Sensitive Estradiol Test
biomarkers.description: Measures estrogen levels to assess ovarian function and hormone balance.
